meta.purpose: R-30 and R-31. Risk for every decision path, including business-as-usual events and black-swan events, and a view on which path best preserves wealth at a manageable level of risk.

scoring_key.likelihood: Qualitative, anchored on verified evidence where any exists. Not a probability.
scoring_key.impact: Share of the asset's value at risk, expressed qualitatively until G-01 and G-08 close.
scoring_key.preventability: Can the owner eliminate this by acting? Yes / Partly / No.

meta.honesty_note: No probability is assigned to any event. Assigning one would be a fabrication in the absence of an insured loss model. The comparisons below are ordinal, not cardinal.

decision_paths.path: Sell now, before the lease term shortens further
decision_paths.summary: Convert an illiquid, single-tenant, deteriorating-credit asset into cash at today's pricing.

decision_paths.path: Market now, close after the tenant's written renewal indication
decision_paths.summary: Use a live market test to discover the price while holding an option to change course.
Trade liquidity for term certainty, wage the bet that the tenant stays and the rent resets.

decision_paths.path: Hold to expiry, then re-let or redevelop
decision_paths.summary: Accept a vacancy period to capture land-value upside at reversion.
Sell the parcel to the tenant and lease it back, or sell subject to its own lease; removes the tenant's rent and can support a higher price.
Defer tax and exchange single-asset concentration for a portfolio of smaller exposures.
Also a decision, and the one most likely to be taken by default.

risks.risk: Tenant closes this unit before lease expiry
risks.evidence: 86 Jack in the Box closures in FY2025, 38 under JACK on Track; FY2026 guidance of 50-100 further closures (S-02). Same-store sales -4.2% FY2025 and -7.4% in Q4 (S-02).
risks.impact: High — rent may continue but the box goes dark, re-letting leverage at expiry collapses, and the buyer pool narrows to land buyers
risks.preventability: No for the closure itself; Partly for the consequences, via lease covenants at renewal
risks.mitigation: Obtain a written renewal indication before renewing. Negotiate a go-dark restriction and a recapture right at first opportunity.

risks.risk: Rent has lost real value and the option rent resets below market
risks.evidence: LA CPI-U grew at 3.79%/yr over 2019-2025 (S-07). A 2% fixed bump against that is roughly a 1.8 point real decline per year, compounding.
risks.likelihood: Depends entirely on the escalation clause — unknown (G-05)
risks.impact: Medium to high over a 5 to 9 year window
risks.preventability: Only at renewal, by negotiating a market reset
risks.mitigation: Close G-05 before renewing; do not renew on the existing mechanism without testing it.

risks.risk: Buyer pool for sub-10-year ground leases is thin and prices a wide spread
risks.evidence: No verified public data. This is a structural feature of net-lease markets, stated here as a reasoned expectation and flagged unverified (I-04).
risks.likelihood: High by construction of the asset
risks.impact: High — this spread is the dominant valuation input
risks.preventability: Partly — selling sooner rather than later keeps the term longer
risks.mitigation: Get three written quotes (G-08) before assuming a price. Selling with more term remaining is generally cheaper than selling with less.

risks.risk: Seismic event damages the building and the land cannot be rebuilt in kind
risks.evidence: The parcel's zone status is unknown (HZ-01 to HZ-04). The region is seismically active; USGS NSHM 2023 is the current model (S-22).
risks.impact: Severe — loss of rent, uninsured repair, and exit liquidity all at once
risks.preventability: Partly — retrofit before the event, insure properly, and avoid holding through a long horizon uninsured
risks.mitigation: Complete HZ-01 to HZ-04, obtain PML, and hold insurance where the deductible is survivable. This risk is the strongest argument against unconditional long-term hold.

risks.risk: California fast-food wage floor rises again and accelerates closures
risks.evidence: Fast-food minimum wage $20.00/hr since 2024-04-01 under AB 1228, with a Fast Food Council empowered to raise it further (S-18). State minimum wage $16.90 from 2026-01-01, indexed to CPI-W capped at 3.5%/yr (S-17). CPI-W 12-month change is 4.1% (S-05).
risks.likelihood: High — the mechanism exists and CPI-W currently runs above the 3.5% cap
risks.impact: Medium — hits the operator's margin, which feeds closure decisions
risks.mitigation: Treat the operator's cost trend as a leading indicator of closure risk and price it into any renewal.

risks.evidence: Not verified this session (HZ-09). Stated as a known structural pressure on California property insurance, flagged as an assumption.
risks.impact: High — an uninsurable building is priced as land
risks.mitigation: Obtain three written insurance indications before marketing (HZ-09).

risks.risk: 1031 replacement is rushed and the owner buys a worse asset
risks.evidence: Statutory identification and acquisition clocks apply (S-15).
risks.likelihood: Moderate whenever the exchange decision is made after the sale
risks.impact: Medium to high — a tax-motivated purchase can destroy more value than the tax saved
risks.mitigation: Identify replacement candidates before listing. Treat 1031 as optional, never as a reason to accept a bad price.

risks.risk: Tax bill arrives larger than expected
risks.evidence: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain at up to 25% (S-12), NIIT 3.8% (S-13), California top marginal 12.3% with no capital-gain preference (S-16).
risks.likelihood: High if basis is low and depreciation was taken
risks.impact: High — can be a fifth or more of gross proceeds
risks.mitigation: Close G-03 and run the calculator before signing anything.

risks.risk: The tenant buys competing supply into the same window
risks.evidence: The tenant's FY2026 guidance explicitly names 'selling real estate' as part of JACK on Track (S-02).
risks.impact: Medium — more supply, same thin buyer pool
risks.mitigation: This cuts both ways: it also means the tenant may be a BUYER (D-5). Price that path.

risks.evidence: MSA nonfarm employment +1.29% versus 2019 and +0.19% versus 2024 (derived from S-06). City population -0.8% since 2020 (S-08). Information -2.1%, Financial Activities -1.6%, Manufacturing -1.2% (S-05).
risks.likelihood: This is the observed state, not a forecast
risks.impact: Medium — caps the growth the hold case depends on
risks.mitigation: Do not underwrite rent growth above verified local inflation.

risks.risk: Vacancy at expiry longer than modelled
risks.likelihood: Moderate to high for a single-purpose box
risks.impact: High — a dark box with a drive-thru is only re-lettable to another QSR until the use is re-permitted
risks.mitigation: Close G-11. If the zoning is single-purpose, the hold case loses most of its reversion argument.

risks.evidence: The owner's other holdings are unknown and not requested. Stated as a structural point.
risks.likelihood: Depends on the owner's balance sheet
risks.impact: Potentially the largest unmodelled risk in the whole analysis
risks.mitigation: State the objective function (G-12). If this asset is a large share of net worth, concentration alone can justify a sale regardless of price.

black_swan_block.summary: Rare events that could destroy the local economy, and what each does to the three stress legs.

events.rent_leg: Rent may continue under the lease but collection is impaired if the operator is displaced.
events.liquidity_leg: Transaction market effectively closes for an extended period.
events.net: The worst combination for a leveraged single asset: cannot sell, must repair, may not collect.

events.event: Urban wildfire reaching dense commercial corridors
events.repair_leg: Rebuild under current code, if the use is permitted at all.
events.liquidity_leg: Insurance withdrawal across the region compresses all values, not just damaged ones.
events.net: Correlated with RS-06, so the insurance leg fails at the same time as the loss.

events.rent_leg: Operator insolvency; rent becomes a claim, not a payment.
events.repair_leg: Deferred maintenance accumulates with no rent to fund it.
events.net: Slow-moving but the most likely of the three to actually occur.

events.event: Regulatory shock to the QSR model
events.net: Partly observable already through the AB 1228 wage mechanism (S-18).

black_swan_block.design_principle: Do not hold a single, illiquid, uninsured-tail asset in a seismic region for a horizon longer than the lease term that justifies it. That is the risk-management conclusion, and it is independent of the price.

best_course_of_action.headline: Conditional, and the condition is sequencing — not a target price.
reasoning: The economic evidence does not support a growth hold. Jobs are +1.29% versus 2019, population is -0.8% since 2020, and only one of nine tracked sectors is clearly growing (Q-25, Q-26, IM-01 to IM-09).

The tenant's own verified disclosures point the wrong way for a renewal: 86 closures, guidance for 50-100 more, same-store sales -4.2% then -7.4%, 7.33x leverage, and a stated plan to sell real estate (TH-01 to TH-22).
The tax code gives a large lever — section 1031 — that only exists if the owner sells while the asset is still a qualifying real-property interest (TX-06).
The black-swan structure penalises a long hold far more than a sale, because it correlates the rent, repair and liquidity legs (RS-04, black_swan_block).
Against all that, the owner's price is unknown and the short-lease discount is unverified (G-08, I-04). Selling without a price is as irresponsible as holding without a plan.

recommended_sequence.action: Close every blocking gate (G-01, G-02, G-03, G-04, G-07, G-12). Nothing else happens first.
recommended_sequence.why: Six unknowns entirely govern the answer.

recommended_sequence.action: Obtain written quotes from three buyers AND a written renewal indication from the tenant, in the same 30-day window.
recommended_sequence.why: This is the only way to compare a real sale price against a real renewal case rather than two templates.

recommended_sequence.action: Ask the tenant, through the broker, whether it will buy the parcel.
recommended_sequence.why: D-5 is the path most likely to produce the highest price and the fewest surprises, and it is almost never tested.

recommended_sequence.action: Run the after-tax number with and without a section 1031 exchange, and identify replacement candidates before listing.
recommended_sequence.why: The tax difference is large enough to change the decision, and the exchange must not be improvised.

recommended_sequence.action: Decide against the owner's written objective function (G-12).
recommended_sequence.why: Sell and hold optimise different things. That trade-off belongs to the owner and cannot be delegated to an analysis.

best_course_of_action.lean_if_forced_today: On the verified evidence, the weight of argument favours selling — but only after gates 1 and 2, and only with the 1031 path prepared in advance. If the objective statement prioritises income over liquidity and the lease has 8+ years of firm term with a strong obligor and a market-reset option, hold becomes defensible. Those two facts are unknown today, which is precisely why the answer is 'not yet'.
what_would_flip_the_recommendation_to_ho: A firm term extending meaningfully past 2032, with no tenant termination right.
A corporate or well-capitalised guaranty behind the rent.
A renewal option with a fair-market-value reset rather than a fixed bump.
Parcel-level hazard findings that are benign, plus affordable insurance.
Zoning headroom that gives the land a credible alternative use.
Three written quotes that come in materially above the owner's hold-case present value.
